title: NEXT F Forms and Leads Contract Registry
description: Generated index of authoritative Phase 8 Forms and Leads definitions.

schemas.name: Form Auto-response
schemas.description: Configures a visitor-facing email response after an accepted submission.
schemas.purpose: Keeps acknowledgement email behavior separate from internal notifications.

fields.description: Form field containing the validated recipient email.

validationRules.description: recipientFieldKey must identify a validated email field.
Auto-response must not be sent before server acceptance.
Sensitive submitted values must not be echoed into the response unless explicitly designed and authorized.
Auto-response must respect anti-abuse/rate-limit controls to avoid becoming a mail relay.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Condition
schemas.description: One declarative condition used by conditional form behavior.
schemas.purpose: Allows safe field-driven visibility without arbitrary JavaScript expressions.

fields.description: Stable key of the field being evaluated.
Comparison value when the operator requires one.

validationRules.description: sourceFieldKey must reference a field in the same Form.
Operators requiring no value must ignore value; all other operators require a compatible value.
Conditions must not contain executable JavaScript or arbitrary expressions.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Condition Group
schemas.description: A safe all/any group of form conditions.
schemas.purpose: Supports deterministic conditional visibility and behavior while limiting complexity.

validationRules.description: A single condition group is limited to a bounded number of conditions.
Phase 8 condition groups do not recursively embed arbitrary nested groups.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Confirmation
schemas.description: Defines what the visitor sees after an accepted form submission.
schemas.purpose: Standardizes success feedback and safe redirects.

fields.description: Safe HTTP(S) redirect destination when mode=redirect.
Whether explicitly allowlisted query parameters may be preserved.

validationRules.description: Only the target appropriate to mode may be populated.
Redirects must use HTTP(S) and may be restricted by Site policy.
Sensitive submitted values must never be placed in redirect query strings.
Success confirmation is shown only after the server accepts the submission.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Consent Field Configuration
schemas.description: Defines what a consent checkbox or acknowledgement means at capture time.
schemas.purpose: Ensures consent capture includes a purpose and stable text/version snapshot rather than a generic untitled checkbox.

fields.description: Whether acceptance is required to submit.

validationRules.description: Consent controls must not be prechecked when an affirmative action is required.
Marketing consent must not be silently bundled into an unrelated required acknowledgement.
This configuration records product behavior and does not by itself establish legal sufficiency in any jurisdiction.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Consent Record
schemas.description: Snapshot of one consent/acknowledgement field at submission time.
schemas.purpose: Preserves what the visitor accepted or declined instead of relying on a later-edited form label.

fields.description: Purpose key captured from field configuration.
Exact consent text shown at submission time.
Policy URL shown at submission time.
Policy version shown at submission time.

validationRules.description: Consent text/version snapshots must not change when the Form is later edited.
accepted must reflect the submitted control state.
The record demonstrates captured system data only and does not itself determine legal validity.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Conversion Mapping
schemas.description: Declares that an accepted form outcome should map to a future registered marketing conversion key.
schemas.purpose: Creates the stable bridge needed for Phase 9 conversions without directly embedding Google, Meta or other vendor tracking code in the Form.

fields.description: Form outcome eligible for conversion mapping.
How a future conversion value is determined.
Optional field key used by a future validated conversion-value mapping.
Whether dispatch to marketing destinations requires marketing consent.

relationships.description: Conversion mapping belongs to a Form.

validationRules.description: conversionKey is a forward reference; canonical conversion/event contracts are introduced in Phase 9 and Phase 13.
This mapping must not contain Google Ads, Meta Pixel or other vendor scripts.
fixedValue/sourceFieldKey usage must match valueMode.
Future marketing dispatch must obey consent and destination rules, not merely this flag.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Data Handling
schemas.description: Controls storage and minimization behavior for form submission data.
schemas.purpose: Makes retention and request-metadata choices explicit before the broader Privacy phase adds jurisdiction-specific policy metadata.

fields.description: Whether accepted submission records are retained.
How source IP information may be handled.
Whether the landing/source page URL is retained.
Whether authorized customer roles may export submissions.

validationRules.description: Only metadata required for the configured business purpose should be retained.
When submissions are stored, retention behavior must be explicit at Site policy level even if retentionDays is inherited.
IP metadata is not a reliable identity or authorization mechanism.
This contract expresses system behavior and does not replace a customer privacy policy or legal review.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Field Mapping
schemas.description: Maps one submitted form field to a registered target field path.
schemas.purpose: Supports predictable lead creation and future integration mapping without executable transformations.

fields.description: Registered target field path, such as lead.displayName.
Whether mapping failure blocks the mapped business action.

validationRules.description: sourceFieldKey must exist in the mapped Form.
targetPath must be explicitly supported by the target mapping contract.
Transformations are limited to registered deterministic operations; arbitrary code is prohibited.
Sensitive source fields require explicit target support and permission-aware handling.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Field Option
schemas.description: One selectable option for select, radio or checkbox-style fields.
schemas.purpose: Provides stable machine values separately from customer-facing labels.

fields.description: Stable machine value submitted by the form.
Whether the option remains visible but cannot be selected.

validationRules.description: Changing an option label must not silently change its stored machine value.
Option values must be unique inside one field.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Field Validation Rule
schemas.description: Declarative validation applied to a form field.
schemas.purpose: Keeps server and client validation intent synchronized without executable custom scripts.

fields.description: Rule parameters appropriate to the rule type.
Localized validation message shown to users.
Registered validator ID when rule=customRegistered; never inline code.

validationRules.description: Every rule affecting acceptance must be enforced server-side; browser validation is UX only.
customRegistered requires a registered server-side validator identifier and must not contain executable code.
parameters must match the selected rule semantics.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form
schemas.description: Complete structured website form definition managed through the Customer CMS.
schemas.purpose: Provides one reusable, code-independent form contract for contact, quote, enquiry, application and lead-generation forms across NEXT F-built websites.

fields.description: Stable form slug/handle where a route/embed requires it.
Ordered directly placed field IDs for simple forms.
Ordered Form Sections for structured single-step forms.
Ordered Form Steps for multi-step forms.
Current immutable revision/version identifier used in new Submission snapshots.

validationRules.description: Form belongs to one Site.
multiStep requires stepIds; singleStep must use fields/sections and not multi-step-only configuration.
Fields participating in stored submissions must preserve their machine keys or use explicit migration/versioning.
Submission processing must validate the submitted formVersion against an allowed/current version policy.
Form definitions must not contain arbitrary HTML, CSS, JavaScript, executable templates or vendor tracking scripts.
Public form rendering exposes only the fields/configuration needed to render and validate the visitor form.
Client validation alone must never create an accepted Submission.
Required consent controls must be positively accepted before acceptance.
Form availability must be checked at server acceptance time.
Anti-abuse and duplicate protections occur before notifications, lead creation or future conversion dispatch.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Availability
schemas.description: Controls whether a form is currently open for submissions.
schemas.purpose: Separates form availability from content publishing and lets a site close or schedule a form without deleting its definition.

fields.description: Message shown when submissions are unavailable.
Whether already-started multi-step sessions may finish after the form closes.

validationRules.description: Scheduled state requires a valid schedule window.
Closed or disabled forms must reject new server-side submission attempts even if a stale frontend remains open.
Form availability is not an authentication or authorization control.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Field
schemas.description: One structured input definition inside a form.
schemas.purpose: Provides the reusable field configuration consumed by the form renderer and submission validator.

fields.description: Stable machine key used in submission snapshots and mappings.
Canonical NEXT F primitive field ID that defines the value shape.
Form-specific visual/input variant without changing stored value semantics.
Whether a valid value is required.
Optional default value matching primitive semantics.
HTML/autofill hint when safe and appropriate.
Presentation hint for the form grid.
Consent semantics when this field represents consent.
Upload restrictions when this is a file field.
Marks the value as requiring stricter operational handling.
Whether the field participates in new submissions.

validationRules.description: key must be unique within one Form and remain stable after submissions exist.
primitiveId must resolve to a registered NEXT F primitive field contract.
options are allowed only for compatible choice input variants.
consent configuration requires an affirmative checkbox/acknowledgement input.
uploadPolicy applies only to file inputs.
Hidden fields are not trusted merely because users cannot see them.
defaultValue must validate against primitiveId and must never pre-accept consent.
Sensitive values must not be copied into logs/events/notification subjects by default.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Section
schemas.description: A semantic grouping of fields within a form or step.
schemas.purpose: Lets CMS authors organize large forms without granting layout-code control.

fields.description: Ordered field IDs in the section.

validationRules.description: Every fieldId must belong to the same Form.
A field must not be placed multiple times in one rendered form unless explicitly supported by a future contract.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Form Step
schemas.description: One ordered step in a multi-step form.
schemas.purpose: Provides predictable multi-step navigation and validation boundaries.

fields.description: Ordered section IDs in this step.
Ordered directly placed field IDs when no section is needed.

validationRules.description: A step must contain at least one field or section.
Referenced sections and fields must belong to the same Form.
Required fields in the current visible step must validate before advancing.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.

schemas.name: Lead
schemas.description: Customer-business lead record created manually, from forms or from future integrations.
schemas.purpose: Provides a lightweight website lead workflow without conflating anonymous submissions, commerce customers or platform organizations.

fields.description: Private contact methods associated with the Lead.

relationships.description: Current status resolves against Site lead statuses.
Lead may be assigned to an actor.

validationRules.description: Lead belongs to one Site and cannot link submissions/users from another tenant without an explicit cross-site platform contract.
Lead contact points are private operational data even though shared.contactPoint can be public in other contexts.
statusKey must resolve to an active or historical forms.leadStatusDefinition for the same Site.
A website Lead is not automatically a Commerce Customer.
A Lead is not the NEXT F customer Organization tenant.
Potential duplicate Leads must follow an explicit deduplication policy instead of silent arbitrary merging.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Activity
schemas.description: Immutable timeline entry describing an operational action on a Lead.
schemas.purpose: Supports a readable lead timeline independently from the future global Event Registry.

validationRules.description: Lead Activity records are append-only operational history.
This timeline model does not define canonical integration events; those are introduced in Phase 13.
Activity metadata must not contain secrets and should minimize personal data.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Assignment
schemas.description: Record of assigning a Lead to an authorized Organization user or team actor.
schemas.purpose: Separates assignment history from the Lead record so ownership changes remain auditable.

validationRules.description: Assignee must be authorized for the Lead Site when permission contracts are introduced.
Changes to assignment must remain auditable and must not rewrite history.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Deduplication Policy
schemas.description: Defines how potential duplicate Leads are detected and handled.
schemas.purpose: Prevents inconsistent ad-hoc merging when repeated form submissions use the same contact details.

fields.description: Action when a candidate match is found.
Whether mapped non-empty lead fields may be overwritten.

validationRules.description: Email/phone matching must use canonical normalized values.
Duplicate handling must not silently destroy historical lead information.
Deduplication indexes/derivatives must be protected and not exposed publicly.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form to Lead Mapping
schemas.description: Defines whether and how accepted Form Submissions create or update Leads.
schemas.purpose: Keeps lead-generation behavior declarative and reusable across NEXT F customer sites.

fields.description: Whether accepted submissions may create/update Leads.
Whether the source submission is linked to the Lead.

relationships.description: Creates or updates Leads after accepted submissions.

validationRules.description: Lead mapping executes only for server-accepted submissions.
Required Lead fields must have valid mappings or controlled defaults.
defaultStatusKey must resolve for the same Site.
defaultAssignee must belong to the authorized Site/Organization scope.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Note
schemas.description: Private note attached to a Lead.
schemas.purpose: Provides a structured private customer-team note without mixing internal commentary into public content.

fields.description: Whether the note is highlighted for the team.

validationRules.description: Lead notes are operational/private and must never be exposed through public site APIs.
A persisted note requires an attributable authorized actor.
Users should not place passwords, API secrets or payment credentials in lead notes.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Source
schemas.description: Provider-neutral source information for a Lead.
schemas.purpose: Records the immediate business source before richer campaign attribution is added by the Marketing phase.

validationRules.description: type=form requires formId.
UTM/ad-platform attribution is not redefined here; it will bind to Phase 9 Marketing contracts.
URLs and external labels must be treated as untrusted metadata.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Lead Status Definition
schemas.description: Site-level configurable lead workflow status.
schemas.purpose: Allows customer businesses to label and order their lead workflow while preserving stable status keys and lifecycle categories.

fields.description: Whether this is the default status for new leads.
Whether this status closes normal active follow-up.
Whether new transitions may target this status.

validationRules.description: Lead status key must be unique per Site.
A Site has at most one active default lead status.
won/lost/closed categories should be configured as closed statuses.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Notification Recipient
schemas.description: A safe recipient definition used by form notification rules.
schemas.purpose: Avoids arbitrary recipient expressions and keeps static addresses separate from field- or user-derived recipients.

validationRules.description: Populate only the recipient field required by type.
formEmailField must resolve to a compatible email field in the same Form.
Resolved email values must be validated and must not allow mail header injection.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Notification Rule
schemas.description: Defines an operational notification after a server-classified submission outcome.
schemas.purpose: Lets customer teams receive submission notifications without embedding mail-provider implementation details in forms.

fields.description: Submission outcome that triggers this rule.
Notification body template using allowlisted placeholders only.
Explicit submission fields allowed in the message.
Whether fields marked sensitive may be included; default false and requires elevated authorization later.

validationRules.description: Templates may interpolate only registered placeholders; arbitrary code/expression execution is prohibited.
Sensitive form values are excluded from notifications by default.
Email/provider credentials and delivery mechanics belong to Integration/API implementation contracts.
A notification rule must enforce recipient-count limits.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Rate Limit Policy
schemas.description: Defines server-side submission throttling for one form.
schemas.purpose: Reduces automated abuse and accidental duplicate submissions without treating rate limiting as authentication.

fields.description: Optional cooldown after a limit is exceeded.

validationRules.description: Rate limits must be enforced server-side.
Rate limiting is an anti-abuse mechanism, not an identity or permission control.
Client-signal storage must respect the Site data-handling/privacy policy.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Submission Request Context
schemas.description: Minimal technical/context metadata captured with a form submission according to Site data-handling policy.
schemas.purpose: Supports diagnostics and source understanding while keeping request metadata separate from business field values.

fields.description: Page URL from which the form was submitted.
Referrer URL when retained and available.
User-agent string only when configured for retention.
Non-reversible or protected client signal derivative used for abuse control when configured.

validationRules.description: Presence of request metadata must follow forms.dataHandling.
Request context must not copy authorization headers, cookies, access tokens or secrets.
Client-provided URLs, locale and user-agent data are untrusted metadata.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Spam Decision
schemas.description: Server-side anti-spam classification for a submission.
schemas.purpose: Keeps spam outcome, score and evidence auditable and separate from the original submitted data.

fields.description: Normalized overall suspicion score when available.
Whether a human review has occurred.

validationRules.description: Authoritative spam decisions are made server-side.
Enough non-secret reasoning should be retained for support/audit review.
Manual reclassification must generate an audit record later under the canonical audit/event system.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Spam Policy
schemas.description: Configures provider-neutral anti-spam controls for a form.
schemas.purpose: Lets sites apply layered abuse controls without binding the Form contract to one CAPTCHA provider.

fields.description: Whether a hidden honeypot signal is used.
Optional maximum link count in free-text fields.
Provider-neutral score threshold when scored signals are available.
Whether an external challenge may be required.
Site-managed abusive terms used as one signal, not the sole security control.

validationRules.description: Spam classification should use multiple signals when practical; honeypots or blocked terms alone are not authoritative.
External CAPTCHA/challenge provider credentials belong to the Integration phase, not this policy.
Spam decisions must be auditable and must not silently delete accepted business records.
Challenges must not unnecessarily block accessible form completion.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Spam Signal
schemas.description: One anti-spam observation attached to a submission.
schemas.purpose: Provides explainable evidence for a spam decision without exposing provider secrets.

fields.description: Normalized suspicion score contribution where applicable.

validationRules.description: Signal reason/provider metadata must not contain challenge secrets, raw tokens or hidden provider credentials.
One signal alone is not necessarily the final spam classification.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Submission
schemas.description: Authoritative server-side record of one form submission attempt/outcome.
schemas.purpose: Preserves validated field snapshots, consent, anti-spam decision and source context independently from later Form edits.

fields.description: Immutable Form/revision version identifier rendered to the visitor.
Retained request context according to policy.

relationships.description: Submission belongs to the Form definition used.
May create or associate a business Lead according to mapping rules.

validationRules.description: status may become accepted only after server-side schema/validation, anti-abuse and required-consent checks.
formVersion must identify the definition used when the visitor submitted.
Accepted submission values and consent snapshots are immutable except explicit redaction/retention operations.
When an idempotency key is used, replay must not create duplicate accepted business effects.
Submission records are never public content.
A Form Submission and a Lead are distinct records; one does not automatically imply the other.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Submission File Reference
schemas.description: Private reference and security state for a file uploaded through a form.
schemas.purpose: Separates submitted file access from public media publishing.

relationships.description: Uses shared media metadata/storage abstraction without public delivery implication.

validationRules.description: A submission upload must never become public merely because it uses shared.mediaAsset.
Blocked or failed-scan files must not be made available to customer download workflows.
Original filename is display metadata only.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Submission Field Value
schemas.description: Immutable snapshot of one submitted field value and its field metadata.
schemas.purpose: Prevents historical submissions from changing meaning when a Form field is renamed or reconfigured.

fields.description: Stable field key at submission time.
Primitive field contract ID at submission time.
Whether the field was marked sensitive.
Whether the stored/displayed value is redacted.

validationRules.description: value must conform to primitiveIdSnapshot unless it is intentionally redacted.
fieldKey, labelSnapshot and primitiveIdSnapshot are immutable after acceptance.
Sensitive values require permission-aware rendering and must not be exposed through public APIs.

delivery.notes: Operational/private by default. Public APIs must not expose this record.

schemas.name: Form Upload Policy
schemas.description: Controls files accepted by one form upload field.
schemas.purpose: Makes file constraints explicit and server-enforceable.

fields.description: Maximum number of files accepted by the field.
Whether server-side security scanning must succeed before the file is usable.

validationRules.description: MIME type, extension and file size restrictions must be enforced server-side.
Original filenames are display metadata and must never determine executable server paths.
When scanning is required, files must remain unavailable to downstream users until scan outcome is clean.
Form-uploaded files are private by default.

delivery.notes: Only the explicitly public rendering subset may be delivered to website visitors.
